added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own two suite arms for the same two test files: baseline fast.log '16 passed in 209.04s' at 4f9a5c76b, after-suite.log '20 passed in 154.14s' EXIT=0 at a7d7483e5; 20-16=4 added, no test that passed at the base fails at the head, so the failure delta is zero.

findings.text: follow-on: the positive arm asserts plant.coil_inductance equals series.T @ plant.section_inductance @ series, but both sides are read back from the same plant and the machine at :255 is built with terminal_scale=1.0, so the supplied terminal already equals the reduction by construction; reinstating the removed guard (keep the terminal as given) leaves the assertion true, so it guards nothing the refusal tests at :267 and :279 do not already guard better.

follow-on: the reconstruction-route arm drives _reduced_machine() (a 2-coil, 4-section fixture) rather than the real ITER sectioned set, so the plan's 'a reconstructed pulse gets a plant for that machine and pulse' is demonstrated only on a reduced winding; the substitution is disclosed in the manifest follow_ons and authorised by the coordinator comment c-s5-plant-vehicle, but the ITER-scale plant driven by a reconstruction remains unbuilt.

follow-on: the baseline suite log carries no header naming a revision, a tree or the command, unlike after-suite.log:1 which names all three, so the '16 passed' baseline cannot be tied to 4f9a5c76b from the log itself; a reader checking the base arm must trust the manifest's assertion rather than the artefact.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit from a6480d72 to a0c3b9f44 -- four commits over five files (71 lines in nova/circuit/coupled_plant.py, 30 in nova/imas/plasma_source.py, 438 in tests/test_coupled_plant.py, and the two doc edits): the generic-source interface, the terminal/section refusal guard and its callable-resolving cache digest, the four arms of tests, and the record splice.
item_verdicts.done_when: the source done_when's three checks are covered -- DINA-unchanged at after-suite.log 'DINA_UNCHANGED max_abs_flux_diff_wb=0.000000000', the reconstruction route at 'RECONSTRUCTION_ROUTE max_rel_flux_diff=1.163e-05 tolerance=1e-03', and the terminal/section guard by tests/test_coupled_plant.py:267/:279 raising 'disagrees with the series reduction' -- but the reconstruction arm drives _reduced_machine(), not the real ITER sectioned plant.
item_verdicts.goal: the source node's goal is to let coupled_plant take a generic plasma source through the source's own interface and to refuse a machine whose supplied terminals disagree with its section block; nova/imas/plasma_source.py:117-145 gives PlasmaSource plasma_times/prescribed_currents/coil_current_times/label and nova/circuit/coupled_plant.py:193-205 refuses the disagreement, so the build lands against the goal.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commits a0c3b9f44/a7d7483e5/42dc8ef43/4f9a5c76b, tests '20 passed in 154.14s' at a7d7483e5, test_logs naming after-suite.log, a negative_control_log at negative-control-flipped-sign-guard-removed.log, a baseline_suite of '16 passed' and an after_suite of '20 passed' so the failure delta is derivable and zero.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the source node's declared scope is the seven paths in its manifest (nova/circuit/coupled_plant.py, tests/test_coupled_plant.py, nova/imas/plasma_source.py, tests/test_plasma_source.py, docs/research/reconstructed-plasma-source.html, docs/evidence/fragments/iter-passive-plasma-circuit/reconstructed-plasma-plant.html and the gate-log directory); the delta touches five of them (tests/test_plasma_source.py unchanged) and nothing outside.

justifications.durability: tests/test_coupled_plant.py:267 and :279 both refuse a machine whose supplied terminal disagrees with its own section reduction and would redden if _require_series_reduction were dropped, but the positive arm at :254 compares plant.coil_inductance against a reduction rebuilt from plant.section_inductance, two sides that move together under the consistent machine :255 feeds in.
justifications.evidence: after-suite.log:1-2 records '20 passed in 154.14s' EXIT=0 with a header naming revision a7d7483e5, tree and command, and the run measures DINA_UNCHANGED 0.000000000 Wb and RECONSTRUCTION_ROUTE 1.163e-05 relative against a predeclared 1e-3, but the baseline arm fast.log carries no header naming a revision or command, so only the manifest ties it to 4f9a5c76b.
justifications.fit: nova/circuit/coupled_plant.py:301 _require_series_reduction follows the module's numpy helper idiom (typed args, np.asarray coercion, a scale-safeguarded compare) and no plan, phase, ticket or version label appears in any added symbol or comment.
justifications.goal_fidelity: nova/imas/plasma_source.py:117 adds prescribed_currents/plasma_times/coil_current_times/label so coupled_plant consumes the source through its own interface, and nova/circuit/coupled_plant.py:193 adds the terminal-equals-series-reduction guard, but check 1 (a reconstructed pulse gets a plant) is exercised only on tests/test_coupled_plant.py:762's _reduced_machine(), not the real ITER sectioned set the plan's coordinator comment names.
justifications.reuse: searched nova/ and scripts/ for an existing terminal/section agreement owner (only nova/circuit/resistance.py:415 series_reduction, which builds a wiring matrix, and coupled_plant.py:344 _reduction_error, which measures modal impedance error, neither of which compares a supplied terminal to its reduction), so the guard is new and PlasmaSource's five new members extend the owner rather than forking it.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff a6480d72..a0c3b9f44 touches exactly the five files the source brief lists (nova/circuit/coupled_plant.py, nova/imas/plasma_source.py, tests/test_coupled_plant.py and the two docs), all inside the declared write paths and with no edit to the not-yours set.
